title: The Blood Price: In Israel, Military Sacrifice Is Becoming Political Power
gist: Religious Zionists now supply roughly 40 percent of Israeli infantry officer school graduates while being 12–14 percent of Jewish Israeli society, and their disproportionate casualties since Oct. 7 have converted military sacrifice into political authority. The practical consequence is that Israeli politicians already treat a West Bank evacuation order as something the army might not execute, narrowing the range of territorial outcomes anyone will contemplate.

themes.theme: Demographic capture of the officer corps

insights.claim: Roughly 40 percent of Israeli infantry officer school graduates now come from the national religious community, which is only 12 to 14 percent of Jewish Israeli society.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The single hardest number in the piece: it quantifies why Israeli territorial policy has a hard institutional floor regardless of who wins elections.
insights.quote: Today, roughly 40 percent of infantry officer school graduates come from the national religious community, which makes up just 12 to 14 percent of Jewish Israeli society.
insights.locator: Israel's New Military Elite

insights.claim: The shift began after the 1973 Yom Kippur War when Israel's secular Ashkenazi elite moved into private-sector and high-technology careers, vacating the combat track.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Israel's tech-sector talent boom and its military's ideological drift are the same story viewed from two ends — a structural, not cyclical, trend.
insights.quote: the traditional elite increasingly pursued careers in the private sector, especially high-technology industries
insights.locator: Israel's New Military Elite

insights.claim: A study in Maarachot, the Israeli Defense Ministry's journal, found a tenfold increase in the share of national-religious infantry officer cadets between 1990 and 2008.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Establishes that the transformation predates Oct. 7 by decades, so it will not reverse when the current war ends.
insights.quote: found a tenfold increase in the share of national-religious infantry officer cadets between 1990 and 2008
insights.locator: Israel's New Military Elite

insights.claim: Hesder yeshivot send roughly 85 percent of their students into combat units and mechinot pre-army academies send graduates into officers' course at three times the national rate.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: These two pipeline institutions, not battlefield chance, are the mechanism producing the officer-corps shift — watch any attempt to regulate them as the key policy fight.
insights.quote: send roughly 85 percent of their students into combat units
insights.locator: Israel's New Military Elite

insights.claim: The proportion of religious settler officers has risen at every rank from platoon commander to general, meaning the change is not confined to junior levels.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Rank-wide penetration means the trend compounds automatically as cohorts age into command.
insights.quote: The proportion of religious settler officers has grown at every level, from platoon commanders to generals.
insights.locator: Israel's New Military Elite

insights.claim: Only 15 percent of religious Zionists supported the 2005 evacuation of 8,000 settlers from Gaza, and the community experienced it as a betrayal by the state itself.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Establishes the grievance baseline that any future evacuation proposal would have to overcome, now multiplied by war casualties.
insights.quote: For religious Zionists, only 15 percent of whom supported the plan, the disengagement was experienced as a betrayal by the state itself.
insights.locator: The turning point came in August 2005

insights.claim: The 2005 evacuation succeeded only because the army deliberately excluded units with high concentrations of religious conscripts, a workaround no longer available.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The precedent everyone cites as proof the army can execute evacuations was engineered around a demographic problem that has since gotten far worse.
insights.quote: in part by deliberately excluding units with high concentrations of religious conscripts, and only about 60 soldiers refused orders
insights.locator: The army carried out the evacuation smoothly

insights.claim: Rabbi Eli Sadan of the Bnei David academy responded to the 2005 defeat by directing religious Zionists to enter the military, Israel Security Agency, Mossad and police to influence them from within, and the community executed that strategy over two decades.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: This is an explicitly stated, documented long-game institutional capture strategy — treat subsequent appointments as its output, not as coincidence.
insights.quote: enter the existing systems of the military, the Israel Security Agency, Mossad, and police
insights.locator: The community drew a strategic lesson from its defeat

insights.claim: Past defense ministers who tried to rein in these religious academies failed, with one minister's removal of a yeshiva from the hesder program reversed by his successor.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Ministerial-level correction has already been tested and failed, so bet against future top-down fixes working.
insights.locator: When past defense ministers tried to rein in such institutions

insights.claim: Rabbi Tzvi Yehuda Kook's messianic teaching that territorial compromise violates God's promise is transmitted as doctrine inside institutions that feed the officer corps.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Ideological content is being institutionalized in the officer-training pipeline, making the constraint doctrinal rather than merely attitudinal.
insights.locator: rooted in the messianic teachings of Rabbi Tzvi Yehuda Kook

insights.claim: Disproportionate national-religious casualties since Oct. 7 have created a moral standing that makes criticism of the community's conduct or political agenda politically costly in Israel.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The central mechanism of the piece: sacrifice is being monetized into policy veto power, which is why Israeli territorial flexibility keeps shrinking.
insights.quote: That sacrifice has become a form of moral authority, and criticism of the community’s conduct or its political agenda now carries a political price.
insights.locator: The Blood Price

insights.claim: Former Israeli military intelligence head Tamir Hayman says officials avoid confronting these incidents for fear of being labeled leftists and attacked on social media, amplified by post-Oct. 7 feelings of hatred and revenge.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: A named senior former official confirming self-censorship inside the security establishment — the constraint is operating, not hypothetical.
insights.quote: People are afraid to confront these incidents because they’d be labeled as leftists and attacked in social media,
insights.locator: The Blood Price

insights.claim: Reserve call-ups exhausted Israel, with religious Zionist turnout staying high while secular participation declined, deepening the sacrifice asymmetry.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The burden gap is widening in real time, so the political asymmetry it produces will keep growing.
insights.locator: As reserve call-ups exhausted the country

insights.claim: Ultra-Orthodox political influence derives from coalition arithmetic while religious Zionist influence derives from battlefield casualties, and the latter is harder for politicians to challenge.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Distinguishes two very different sources of veto power; coalition-based leverage can be bargained away, sacrifice-based leverage cannot.
insights.quote: But that influence comes from coalition politics, not the battlefield.
insights.locator: The obvious objection is that Israel's ultra-Orthodox

insights.claim: In the Haredi draft exemption fight, some of the strongest criticism of ultra-Orthodox demands comes from religious Zionists who believe they bore the greatest war burden.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The right-wing bloc is not monolithic: the draft-exemption issue is an internal fracture line that could destabilize coalitions.
insights.locator: In the battle over the Haredi draft exemption

insights.claim: Scholar Elisheva Rosman-Stollman argues religious Zionists felt they made the ultimate sacrifice by complying with the 2005 evacuation only to see it completely brushed aside by Israel's leadership.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Explains why compliance is unlikely to be repeated: the community concluded that obedience earned it nothing.
insights.quote: completely brushed aside
insights.locator: Elisheva Rosman-Stollman, a scholar of religion

insights.claim: Two summer 2024 appointments — Brig. Gen. Yehuda Vach to the Netzarim corridor division and Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth to Central Command — placed Bnei David graduates in the two commands most relevant to Gaza and West Bank policy.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence the two-decade infiltration strategy has reached operational command of the disputed territories.
insights.locator: Two appointments made in the summer of 2024

insights.claim: A Haaretz investigation found Vach opposed facilitating humanitarian aid and moved on his own initiative to clear northern Gaza, described as a kind of army within an army.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Command-level autonomy means humanitarian and operational outcomes are less predictable from Israeli cabinet policy than outside observers assume.
insights.quote: a kind of army within an army
insights.locator: An Army Within an Army

insights.claim: Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth established formal coordination with settlers building illegal outposts in the West Bank, the very activity his troops nominally police.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Formal army-settler coordination institutionalizes outpost expansion, raising the cost and unlikelihood of any future reversal.
insights.locator: became head of Central Command in the West Bank

insights.claim: Scholar Tomer Persico reports religious Zionist-led units enjoyed unusual autonomy with commanders who would basically do whatever they wanted.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Chain-of-command erosion is a distinct risk from ideology: it makes escalation events harder to attribute or control.
insights.quote: would basically do whatever they wanted
insights.locator: An Army Within an Army

insights.claim: Former Israeli military chief psychologist Reuven Gal says many religious soldiers saw the Gaza campaign as a holy war, and one Sde Teiman abuse defendant justified himself by quoting that week's Torah portion rather than military regulations.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Religious law substituting for military regulation as the operative authority is the clearest sign of doctrinal displacement inside the ranks.
insights.quote: holy war
insights.locator: Lower down the ranks

insights.claim: 65 percent of Israelis now believe the Purity of Arms doctrine prevents the army from fulfilling its mission, roughly double the share of a decade ago, per the Israel Democracy Institute.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Public opinion has moved decisively against restraint doctrine, removing the domestic constituency that once backed the high command.
insights.quote: 65 percent of Israelis now believe the Purity of Arms doctrine prevents the army from fulfilling its mission, roughly double the share of a decade ago
insights.locator: The Spirit of the Israel Defense Forces

insights.claim: Dozens of prominent rabbis signed a letter declaring no religious barrier to bombing hospitals where the enemy shelters, directly contesting the army's ethical code.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Rabbinic authority is being asserted as a competing source of targeting legitimacy against the military chain of command.
insights.locator: Prominent rabbis have circulated the claim

insights.claim: Hours after Oct. 7 the Israeli military authorized officers to strike low-ranking Hamas fighters even at risk of killing up to 20 civilians, a threshold previously reserved for high-value targets, per the New York Times.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: A specific, quantified rules-of-engagement shift that anchors the legal-exposure debate around the Gaza campaign.
insights.locator: The New York Times reported that hours after the Oct. 7 attacks

insights.claim: The high command has not surrendered: Zamir suspended the entire Netzah Yehuda battalion over the West Bank outpost incident and Halevi defended disciplining soldiers over the Jenin mosque episode against far-right attacks.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The counterweight is real but resides in individuals rather than institutions, making it vulnerable to personnel turnover.
insights.locator: To be sure, the high command has not given up on the code.

insights.claim: When the military disciplines soldiers for crossing the line, cabinet members have repeatedly sided with the disciplined rather than the commanders imposing discipline.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Political backing of indiscipline is what converts isolated incidents into a durable norm shift.
insights.locator: Second, when the military has disciplined soldiers

insights.claim: Generals currently enforcing restraint norms were formed by an earlier army while the cadets sitting through politicized lectures will command brigades within a decade, so the trend has a built-in generational clock.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Gives a rough time horizon — roughly ten years — after which the institutional counterweight to religious-nationalist doctrine largely disappears.
insights.quote: the cadets now sitting through lectures like Winter’s will be commanding brigades within the next decade
insights.locator: Two factors point in the opposite direction.

insights.claim: Nearly 40 percent of Israelis now support annexing Gaza, three times the size of the religious Zionist community that traditionally championed the idea.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The settlement agenda has escaped its original constituency and gone mainstream, materially reducing the probability of a negotiated Gaza settlement.
insights.quote: Polls now show nearly 40 percent of Israelis supporting Gaza’s annexation, three times the size of the religious Zionist community that traditionally championed it.
insights.locator: The Politics of Sacrifice

insights.claim: More than half a million settlers now live in the West Bank on land religious Zionists regard as the biblical heartland, and the army can no longer assign an evacuation to secular units because its combat core is drawn from the community that would be evacuated.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The mechanical reason a two-state outcome has become far less executable regardless of diplomatic pressure.
insights.quote: The settler population there exceeds half a million
insights.locator: The stakes are higher in the West Bank

insights.claim: An officer quoted in an International Crisis Group report vowed to resist any withdrawal order by all legitimate means and, if that were insufficient, by illegitimate means, showing refusal rhetoric has been normalized.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Open, on-record refusal talk from serving officers is the observable signal that the constraint has moved from theory to expectation.
insights.quote: by all legitimate means, and if that isn’t enough, by illegitimate means
insights.locator: The rhetoric of refusal, meanwhile

insights.claim: Whether the army would actually fracture under an evacuation order is unknowable, but Israeli politicians already behave as though it would, which is what has narrowed the range of territorial outcomes on the table.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: The key analytical move: the anticipation, not the test, is the binding constraint — so no diplomatic initiative can resolve it by proving the army loyal.
insights.quote: Whether that authority is ever tested by an actual evacuation order matters less than the fact that Israeli politicians already treat it as a constraint.
insights.locator: The Israeli military has long been Israel's chief integrating institution

insights.claim: Settler organizations began campaigning within weeks of Oct. 7 to rebuild the Gush Katif settlements, with Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich signing a Victory Pact committing to Gaza's resettlement over Netanyahu's dismissal of the idea as unrealistic.
insights.speaker: Guy Ziv
insights.so_what: Coalition-internal pressure on Netanyahu on Gaza resettlement is sustained and formalized, limiting his room to accept postwar arrangements.
insights.quote: God willing, together we will settle and be victorious,
insights.locator: The Politics of Sacrifice
